balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Wipro Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Wipro Limited: the headline cash balance includes a large book of mutual funds, certificates of deposit and other investments that Wipro's filings disclose separately from pure cash only (bank balances and deposits). The gap between the two bars is that investment book, not liquidity risk -- but it means the headline figure overstates what is instantly callable.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • How much of "cash" is actually the investment portfolio versus bank cash
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

bookings.title: Bookings and large deal TCV
bookings.content:
Total bookings is the value of new contracts signed in the quarter; large deal TCV (total contract value) is the subset from deals large enough to be individually disclosed, usually multi-year.

For Wipro Limited: bookings lead revenue by roughly one to three quarters in IT services. The Q2 FY2027 guidance cut was attributed directly to a weak prior-quarter bookings print, and large deal TCV swings quarter to quarter even when the broader book is healthy because a handful of mega-deals can dominate the number.

What to watch:

  • Bookings growth outrunning (or lagging) revenue growth -- a leading signal either way
  • Large deal TCV concentration: a few deals driving most of the total
  • Book-to-bill ratio (bookings ÷ revenue) trending below 1x

attrition.title: IT services attrition rate
attrition.content:
Attrition is the trailing-twelve-month voluntary attrition rate among IT services staff -- the share of the workforce that leaves each year.

For Wipro Limited: attrition is a direct cost and delivery-risk lever in a people-heavy offshore model: every departure means backfill hiring, training cost and billing disruption on client accounts. Wipro's rate fell from the post-pandemic talent-war peak (above 20% industry-wide in 2022) into the low teens by FY2025-27, which eases wage inflation but also signals a slower hiring market.

What to watch:

  • Direction versus peers (TCS, Infosys, HCLTech) -- a rate rising alone, against the sector falling, is company-specific
  • Attrition versus net headcount adds: low attrition with shrinking headcount means demand softness, not retention success
  • Wage-hike cycles that typically follow a period of elevated attrition

activeCustomers.title: Active clients
activeCustomers.content:
Active clients is the count of enterprise customers Wipro reports as active, disclosed once a year.

For Wipro Limited: IT services revenue is dominated by the largest existing accounts, so client-count growth matters less on its own than revenue per client and the mix of $100m+ accounts -- but a falling count alongside flat or falling revenue flags client losses the growth numbers don't yet show.

What to watch:

  • Client count versus revenue growth -- are the same clients spending more, or is the base shrinking
  • Count of $100m+ and $50m+ strategic accounts (disclosed separately in filings) as a concentration check

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Wipro Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Wipro Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Wipro Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Wipro Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Wipro Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Wipro Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Wipro Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Wipro Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
